kszq1h: Quarks Science Club is a non-profit social organization dedicated to transforming basic education in Sergipe through innovation in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics). Made up of a multidisciplinary team of researchers, PhDs and young scientists, we combine technical rigor and creativity to turn the classroom into a true living lab, where science education becomes accessible, tangible and inspiring.
1u4037e: We move beyond lecture-based traditionalism by applying the “hands-on” methodology. We develop low-cost experimental kits, software and teaching materials aligned with the BNCC and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Our work goes beyond theory: we bring maker culture to subjects such as Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with ongoing training that strengthens teachers' autonomy.
t3l768: One of our main differentiators is our commitment to legacy. Unlike traditional consultancies, we transfer the intellectual property and the technology we develop to the school itself. This ensures financial sustainability and makes hands-on learning an everyday practice, not just an exception.
1wlw4xs: Our goal is to make Sergipe the largest center for training tech-minded people in Brazil's Northeast. Through strategic partnerships and structural projects, we connect cutting-edge academic knowledge to everyday school life, paving the way for young people from Sergipe to lead the future and for science to act as a real engine of social development.

xayk4m: The “Sustainable Energy Is Fundamental” project, carried out in partnership with CONCESE, promoted science and environmental education in public schools in Aracaju and Simão Dias. It delivered low-cost experiment kits covering ten different topics, including Electrostatics, Electromagnetism, Power Generation and Electrical Hazards. It also included teacher training and technical visits, such as to the Xingó Hydroelectric Plant. The methodology used experimentation to connect the curriculum to everyday life, resulting in science fairs and the publication of 12 teaching books.
